q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
Today is August 22, 2026. NVIDIA will release Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026 (4 days from now). The forward guidance will be announced at that time, so resolution occurs in approximately 4 days.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release. Based on the research provided, NVIDIA has already provided Q2 FY2027 revenue guidance of **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (range: $89.2B to $92.8B).

When companies report quarterly earnings, they typically provide guidance for the *next* quarter. Since Q2 FY2027 guidance has already been issued (before the August 26 earnings call), the question is asking what guidance will be provided for **Q3 FY2027** at that earnings call.

Key context:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6B (85% YoY growth, 20% sequential growth)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0B ± 2% (representing 11.4% sequential growth from Q1's $81.6B)
- Current Wall Street consensus for Q2: ~$91.9B (within NVIDIA's guidance range)
- Historical context: NVIDIA has shown ~20% sequential growth Q1→Q2

The most likely scenario is that NVIDIA will guide for **Q3 FY2027** revenue in a range that reflects:
1. Continued strong data center demand (their primary driver)
2. Typical sequential growth patterns (though potentially moderating from 20% as they reach higher absolute levels)
3. Potential seasonal variations

If Q2 comes in near consensus (~$91.9B), and assuming 12-16% sequential growth to Q3 (moderating from the 20% Q1→Q2 growth), Q3 FY2027 guidance would likely be in the range of **$103-107B**.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Weaker-than-expected demand signals** for AI infrastructure
- **Increased China revenue restrictions** that exceed current expectations
- **Competitive pressure** from AMD or custom chips reducing NVIDIA's TAM
- **Macro slowdown** affecting cloud provider capex decisions
- **Supply chain disruptions** limiting production
- **Lower-than-guidance Q2 results** indicating demand softening
- **Conservative guidance** from management as a risk management practice

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Better-than-expected Q2 results** (beating the $91B guidance)
- **Accelerating AI adoption** driving higher-than-expected capex spending
- **New product launches** (Blackwell ramping faster than expected)
- **Unexpected strong demand** from emerging data center applications (AI inference expansion)
- **Expansion into new markets** or customer segments beyond hyperscalers
- **Upside surprise from international markets**
- **Aggressive/optimistic forward guidance** reflecting management confidence

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 to Q2 FY2027: 11.4% sequential growth ($81.6B → $91.0B guidance)
- Q4 FY2026 to Q1 FY2027: 20% sequential growth ($68B implied → $81.6B)
- Year-over-year growth: 85% in Q1, implying ~96-97% for Q2 (Q2 FY2026 was $46.7B)

NVIDIA's recent sequential growth has ranged from 11-20%. As the company reaches larger absolute revenue figures, sequential growth rates typically moderate. A reasonable expectation for Q3 FY2027 guidance would be 10-15% sequential growth from the $91B Q2 baseline, suggesting a range of **$100.1B to $104.7B**.

Given that:
1. The forecast range provided (99.5B to 115.5B) is quite wide
2. Consensus expectations center around $91.9B for Q2 (suggesting Q3 guidance around $102-105B)
3. NVIDIA's guidance tends to be conservative relative to actual results
4. Sequential moderation from 20% to ~12-13% is realistic

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, after market close [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).

For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, an 85% increase year-over-year and 20% sequentially [nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). Data Center revenue reached $75.2 billion, up 92% year-over-year [nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).

NVIDIA's guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is approximately $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which is within NVIDIA's guidance range (floor near $89.2 billion, ceiling near $92.8 billion) [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This implies a year-over-year revenue close to doubling from the $46.7 billion reported in Q2 FY2026 [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
